note: Files in src/ that may read the process environment directly. Each entry: "<path>": "why this file owns process env access". Everything else reads the scope's env view, and child processes get theirs from indus.safety.child_env.

allow.src/indus/foundation/bootstrap.py: process bootstrap: chooses the profile and writes INDUS_HOME/scratch vars before any scope exists
allow.src/indus/foundation/envload.py: publish_to_process: the single-profile CLI entry publishes its env view to the process once
allow.src/indus/foundation/home.py: home resolution runs before a scope exists; callers can pass an env mapping instead
allow.src/indus/foundation/scope.py: EnvView.from_process: the one snapshot of the process env every scope starts from
allow.src/indus/platform/facts.py: platform probes sit below foundation (no scope); the process env is only the default when no mapping is passed
allow.src/indus/platform/locate.py: executable lookup sits below foundation (no scope); the process env is only the default when no mapping is passed
allow.src/indus/state/connection.py: test-isolation guard (R03.24) must see the real process env markers; callers can pass a mapping
allow.src/indus/state/doctor_report.py: module entry point: reads the process env to report how the profile was selected, before bootstrap
